title: Nocturne in E-flat major, Op. 9 No. 2 (opening)
description: Chopin's most famous nocturne: a bel canto melody in 12/8 over a rocking waltz-like bass, decorated more lavishly each time it returns. Learning the opening teaches cantabile voicing, left-hand leaps, and how to fit ornamental runs freely over a steady accompaniment.

arrangements.label: Pro
arrangements.notes: Chopin's text for the pickup and bars 1-16 (theme, ornamented theme, the B section and the return of the theme), with the grace notes written out as 32nds (bar 8 acciaccatura, bar 13 grace triplet, trill terminations in bars 7 and 15) and the Schirmer fingerings.
teachingPoints: Left hand: each beat is bass note then two chords; the bass alternates registers (Eb2, Eb3, Eb2, D2 in bar 1), so practise the leaps slowly with the eyes on the bass note.
Bars 1-4 are the plain theme: finger 5-4 substitution on the opening G5, and the Bb4 upbeats with the thumb; keep the melody singing above the pp chords.

Bar 6 and 14 (the chromatic ascent B-C, Db-C, F-E, Ab-G, Db-C) and the 32nd runs in bar 16 are played freely over a left hand that does not slow down; practise hands separately, then fit the run into the two accompaniment chords.
Bars 11-12: the right hand plays dyads and triads; the chromatic bass in bar 12 (Bb-A-G#-G-F-Bb) drives into the Tempo I return at bar 13.
Bars 7, 10 and 15: the trill on F (finger 2-3) ends with E-F before the staccato G; bar 10's four staccato Ebs are a poco ritardando into the dominant.
